prompt_text: Who is the best dentist in Columbus Ohio for a dental implant?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” dentist for implants — the right provider depends on your needs (complexity of the case, medical history, bone loss, desired timeline, budget, sedation needs) and the clinician’s training and experience. Instead of one name, here’s how to find the best implant provider in Columbus and what to look for.

Which type of clinician?
- Oral & maxillofacial surgeons (OMS): typically handle surgical placement, complex cases, bone grafts and sinus lifts.  
- Periodontists: specialists in gums and supporting structures; skilled at implant placement and bone grafting.  
- Prosthodontists or restorative dentists: design and place the final crown/bridge on the implant and manage the overall restorative plan. Good implant care often involves a team approach (surgeon or perio + restorative dentist).

Credentials and experience to check
- Specialist training (oral surgeon, periodontist, prosthodontist) or extensive implant-focused continuing education.  
- Board certification or Diplomate status (e.g., American Board of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgery, American Board of Periodontology, American Board of Prosthodontics, or AAID credentials).  
- Years and number of implants placed, and experience with cases like yours (immediate implants, full-arch, severe bone loss).  
- Use of 3D imaging (CBCT) and digitally guided implant placement.  
- Implant systems they use (Nobel, Straumann, Zimmer, etc.) — reputable manufacturers and availability of parts long-term.  
- Before/after photos and patient references or reviews.

Questions to ask at a consultation
- How many implants do you place per year and how many of this specific type of case?  
- Will you perform any grafts or sinus lifts if I need them? What’s the timeline?  
- Who will do the restoration (implant crown/bridge)? Is that person part of this practice or an outside dentist?  
- Do you use CBCT and guided surgery? Can I see case photos or patient references?  
- What are the risks, success rate, and expected timeline? Is there a warranty/guarantee and what follow-up care is included?  
- Sedation options and cost/financing.

How to find candidates in Columbus
- Use professional directories: AAOMS (oral surgeons), AAP (periodontists), AAID (implant dentists), or the local dental society.  
- Check credentials on the Ohio Dental Board.  
- Read Google/Yelp/Healthgrades reviews and look for consistent patterns (not just isolated good/bad reviews).  
- Consider academic centers: The Ohio State University College of Dentistry / Wexner Medical Center offers specialist-level care and handles complex cases.  
- Ask your general dentist for referrals — they often refer to trusted specialists and coordinate the restorative work.

If you’d like, I can:
- Give a short list of well-reviewed implant specialists and academic options in Columbus if you want me to look them up (I’ll need permission to search now).  
- Help you evaluate 2–3 names you already have in mind — give me their names and I’ll list questions and what to check.

Which would you prefer?
